facts.statement: Guizhouichthyosaurus lived during the Late Triassic period in southwest China.
facts.quote: Guizhouichthyosaurus is an extinct genus of ichthyosaur which is known primarily from the Xiaowa Formation of the lower Carnian stage of the Late Triassic in southwest China.

facts.statement: Fossils of Guizhouichthyosaurus have also been found in the Middle Triassic Zhuganpo Formation.
facts.quote: The genus is also known from the Ladinian-aged Middle Triassic Zhuganpo Formation

facts.statement: Guizhouichthyosaurus was a large ichthyosaur, typically about 5 meters long, with some specimens exceeding 6 meters.
facts.quote: Guizhouichthyosaurus is a large ichthyosaur, typically measuring approximately 5 m long with some specimens exceeding 6 m.

facts.statement: Guizhouichthyosaurus had a long, powerful snout and a low sagittal crest on the back of its skull.
facts.quote: The snout is long and powerful, and there is a low sagittal crest on the rear part of its skull.

facts.statement: Guizhouichthyosaurus possessed a tail bent downwards at the end, sickle-shaped shoulder blades, and an opening between each set of lower leg bones.
facts.quote: The tail is bent downwards near its end, the scapulae (shoulder blades) are shaped like sickles, and an opening is enclosed between each set of lower leg bones.

facts.statement: Each limb of Guizhouichthyosaurus contained at least four digits.
facts.quote: Each limb contains a minimum of four digits.

facts.statement: Guizhouichthyosaurus likely used eel-like swimming, which was less efficient than the cod- or tuna-like swimming of later ichthyosaurs.
facts.quote: Guizhouichthyosaurus, like other early ichthyosaurs, would have used anguilliform (eel-like) locomotion, unlike the more efficient cod- and tuna-like swimming of later ichthyosaurs.

facts.statement: Despite having small, smooth-edged teeth, Guizhouichthyosaurus was an apex predator capable of eating other large marine reptiles, as shown by a thalattosaur skeleton found in its stomach region.
facts.quote: Despite its small, smooth-edged teeth, Guizhouichthyosaurus is known to have been able to consume other large marine reptiles, as evidenced from a thalattosaur skeleton in the stomach region of one specimen, indicating that Guizhouichthyosaurus was an apex predator.

facts.statement: Guizhouichthyosaurus was previously reassigned to the genus Shastasaurus but is now considered a distinct genus.
facts.quote: It has been reassigned as a species of the genus Shastasaurus in the past, though it has since been considered distinct.

facts.statement: A 2011 study by P. Martin Sander and colleagues concluded that Guizhouichthyosaurus was quite distinct from Shastasaurus.
facts.quote: A 2011 paper by P. Martin Sander and colleagues considered Guizhouichthyosaurus to be quite distinct from Shastasaurus

facts.statement: Some reported specimens of Guizhouichthyosaurus reached a total length of around 7 meters.
facts.quote: Additionally, specimens of Guizhouichthyosaurus reaching around 7 m in total length have also been reported.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the species Callawayia wolonggangense belongs to Guizhouichthyosaurus, as recent studies found no traits unambiguously linking it to that genus.
facts.quote: However, they found no traits unambiguously linking it to Guizhouichthyosaurus either, thus also rejected its assignment to that genus.

facts.statement: Guizhouichthyosaurus possessed a long and powerful snout.
facts.quote: Guizhouichthyosaurus has a long, powerful snout.

facts.statement: The teeth of Guizhouichthyosaurus were conical with blunted tips and set in sockets.
facts.quote: The teeth of Guizhouichthyosaurus are conical, have somewhat blunted tips, and are set into sockets.

facts.statement: Each tooth of Guizhouichthyosaurus had 3 to 5 fine vertical ridges but no cutting edges.
facts.quote: They have 3 to 5 very fine vertical ridges, but lack cutting edges.

facts.statement: Guizhouichthyosaurus had approximately 65 vertebrae before the hips and 2 hip vertebrae.
facts.quote: There are about 65 vertebrae in front of the hips in Guizhouichthyosaurus, followed by 2 hip vertebrae.

facts.statement: Guizhouichthyosaurus had an elongated tail with around 170 vertebrae that bent sharply downward near the tip.
facts.quote: The tail of Guizhouichthyosaurus is elongate, containing around 170 vertebrae, and is abruptly bent downwards near its end.

facts.statement: The shoulder blades of Guizhouichthyosaurus were wide, asymmetrical, sickle-shaped, and lacked constricted bases.
facts.quote: The wide scapulae (shoulder blades) are asymmetrical, sickle-shaped, and lack constricted bases.

facts.statement: The interclavicle bone in Guizhouichthyosaurus was shaped like the letter T.
facts.quote: The interclavicle (a shoulder bone between the collarbones) is shaped like the letter T.

facts.statement: Guizhouichthyosaurus had four primary digits (digits II to V) in both its forefins and hindfins, though accessory digits might have been present.
facts.quote: Both the forefins and hindfins of Guizhouichthyosaurus have four primary digits, in both cases representing digits II to V, but additional accessory digits may be present.

facts.statement: A 2013 study divided well-preserved specimens of Guizhouichthyosaurus into two morphotypes, Type A and Type B, which researchers considered variations of the same species.
facts.quote: A 2013 study by Shang and Li found that all specimens of Guizhouichthyosaurus with sufficient good preservation could be divided into two morphotypes, though they were all sufficiently similar to belong to the same species.

facts.statement: Researchers suggested the two morphotypes of Guizhouichthyosaurus likely represented sexual dimorphism rather than growth stages, as there was no significant size difference between them.
facts.quote: Since there was no significant difference in skull or body size between the two types, Shang and Li rejected that the differences were due to growth, and instead considered that they most likely represented differences between males and females.

facts.statement: Researchers hypothesized that Type A individuals were females due to their longer trunks and shorter tails, a trait seen in modern lizards, though this was not confirmed by pregnant specimens.
facts.quote: Since members of type A have proportionately longer trunks and shorter tails than type B, the researchers considered type A to be the females, although no pregnant specimens are known to confirm this.

facts.statement: A 2019 study used computational fluid dynamics to model the swimming energy demands of Guizhouichthyosaurus alongside eight other ichthyosaur taxa.
facts.quote: In 2019, Susana Gutarra and colleagues studied the energy demands of swimming in ichthyosauriforms using computational fluid dynamics and models of nine taxa, one of which was Guizhouichthyosaurus.

facts.statement: Guizhouichthyosaurus generated more drag than other studied ichthyosaurs due to its large flippers.
facts.quote: Guizhouichthyosaurus, in addition to Chaohusaurus, produced more drag than the other taxa, due to their large flippers.

facts.statement: Triassic ichthyosaurs like Guizhouichthyosaurus likely used eel-like swimming, whereas later species evolved more efficient cod-like or tuna-like swimming styles.
facts.quote: Additionally, while Triassic ichthyosaurs such as Guizhouichthyosaurus would have used anguilliform (eel-like) locomotion, later ichthyosaurs switched to the more efficient carangiform (cod-like) and thunniform (tuna-like) swimming styles.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the morphological differences between Type A and Type B Guizhouichthyosaurus represent sexual dimorphism, as no pregnant specimens exist to confirm the hypothesis that Type A are females.
facts.quote: Since members of type A have proportionately longer trunks and shorter tails than type B, the researchers considered type A to be the females, although no pregnant specimens are known to confirm this.

facts.statement: The gastroliths found in the specimen vary in size from 0.6 to 3.7 cm in diameter and are generally round.
facts.quote: These stones vary in size from 0.6 to 3.7 cm in diameter and generally are rather round.

facts.statement: Researchers found that the roughly 1 kilogram of gastroliths was insufficient to serve as ballast for an animal that could weigh as much as a ton.
facts.quote: Cheng and colleagues found the roughly 1 kilogram of stones to be insufficient to usefully serve as ballast for an animal potentially weighing as much as a ton.

facts.statement: A specimen of Guizhouichthyosaurus contains the preserved torso and limbs of a thalattosaur named Xinpusaurus.
facts.quote: The Guizhouichthyosaurus sp. specimen XNGM-WS-50-R4 contains the torso and limbs of the thalattosaur Xinpusaurus, another marine reptile.

facts.statement: A specimen of G. tangae preserves fish bones and bivalves in its stomach region, indicating it ate other prey besides large marine reptiles.
facts.quote: Guizhouichthyosaurus ate other prey items as well, as evidenced by a G. tangae specimen preserving fish bones as well as some bivalves in its stomach region.

facts.statement: Guizhouichthyosaurus had small teeth without cutting edges, which were suitable for holding prey like cephalopods rather than cutting them.
facts.quote: Unlike a typical predator of large animals, the teeth of Guizhouichthyosaurus are rather small and do not have cutting edges, suitable for holding on to prey items like cephalopods.

facts.statement: Researchers hypothesized that the Guizhouichthyosaurus died soon after consuming its large prey.
facts.quote: Jiang and colleagues hypothesized that soon after eating its prey, the ichthyosaur died.

facts.statement: Guizhouichthyosaurus was apparently a generalist feeder.
facts.quote: Guizhouichthyosaurus was apparently a generalist feeder.

facts.statement: Guizhouichthyosaurus was a large ichthyosaur that fed by suction, helping it catch invertebrates, shell-less cephalopods, and fish with its narrow, completely toothless snout.
facts.quote: Guizhouichthyosaurus era un gran ictiosaurio que se alimentaba por succión, lo que le ayudaba a cazar invertebrados marinos, cefalópodos sin caparazón y peces con su hocico estrecho y completamente desdentado, ya que los dientes ya no eran necesarios para capturar este tipo de presas.

facts.statement: Guizhouichthyosaurus had an ecological niche similar to modern humpback whales, with reduced tail flippers and a relatively small head compared to its body.
facts.quote: Por tanto Guizhouichthyosaurus tenía un nicho ecológico similar al de las actuales ballenas jorobadas, sus aletas caudales estaban reducidas y su cabeza era relativamente pequeña en comparación a su cuerpo.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the gastrolith clusters were stored by the animal or formed after death, with some researchers suggesting the stones may have killed the animal by clogging its intestines.
facts.quote: Cheng and colleagues doubted that Guizhouichthyosaurus would have been stored them in two different regions, a configuration seen in no other vertebrate. Instead, they speculated that the clusters formed after death, or even that some gastroliths might have killed the animal after moving into and clogging its intestines.

facts.statement: The function of gastroliths is controversial, with some suggesting buoyancy control, though researchers argue the stones were insufficient for ballast in a large animal.
